title: KU MT14 Virologisk Center - Totalrådgivning
description: Bygningsstyrelsen udbyder en aftale om totalrådgivning vedrørende etablering af Virologisk Center i en eksisterende bygning til brug for Det Sundhedsvidenskabelige Fakultet (SUND) ved Københavns Universitet (KU). Virologisk Center skal etableres som en laboratoriefacilitet til forskning i virus tilhørende risikogruppe 2 og 3 (BSL3) samt arbejde med genetisk modificerede virus klassificeret som GMO klasse 2 (GMO2). Laboratoriefaciliteten skal udføres som en indeslutningsfacilitet, der kan godkendes og klassificeres til BSL3- og GMO2-niveau. Faciliteten skal overholde krav i danske regelsæt og herudover skal relevante internationale manualer, standarder, guidelines samt best practice på området inddrages og lægges til grund – såvel metodemæssigt i form analyser, risiko- og kvalitetsstyring som i form af løsningsvalg, udførelse og verifikation heraf. Projektets specialiserede karakter forudsætter derfor stærke rådgivningskompetencer generelt - og herunder specialistkompetencer inden for biocontainment - med indgående erfaring fra tilsvarende byggerier samt kendskab til gældende danske og internationale krav til BSL3-laboratorier. Projektet omfatter et bruttoareal på ca. 520 m². Projektet forventes gennemført med tidlig inddragelse af en leverandør af barrieresystem, mens øvrige arbejder forventes udbudt i 1-2 storentrepriser med Bygningsstyrelsen som bygherre og Københavns Universitet som bruger. Anslået værdi for kontrakt: 35 mio. kr. Der er tale om et ikke-bindende skøn baseret på Bygningsstyrelsens nuværende budgetforudsætninger. Der henvises i øvrigt til udbudsmaterialet. Udbudsbetingelserne indeholder en nærmere beskrivelse af opgaven og udbudsforløbet, og det øvrige materiale indeholder en beskrivelse af opgavens omfang

title: Germany – Contractor's all-risk insurance services – Projektversicherung für das Projekt Herstellung Zweigleisigkeit Strecke 6142, Abschnitt Lübbenau-Cottbus
description: Die DB InfraGO AG plant den 2-gleisigen Ausbau der Strecke Lübbenau-Cottbus. Projektinhalt der Gesamtmaßnahme ist der zweigleisige Ausbau der Strecke 6142 (Berlin – Görlitz) im Abschnitt Lübbenau (a) – Cottbus (a) von km 85,325 bis km 112,500, der bislang lediglich ein Gleis aufweist. Das Bauvorhaben wird in zwei antragsgegenständliche Planfeststellungsabschnitte gegliedert. Deren Grenze ist die Kreisgrenze zwischen den Landkreisen Oder-Spreewald-Lausitz und Spree-Neiße. Die Investitionssumme für dieses Projekt wird mit EUR 365 Mio. veranschlagt. Hiervon sind bereits ca. EUR 30 Mio. über einen bestehenden Vertrag abgerechnet worden. Der hier neu ausgeschriebene Versicherungsvertrag wird den bestehenden Vertrag ablösen. Es wird mit einer derzeit geplanten Bauzeit bis zum 30.06.2028 gerechnet. Der Versicherungsvertrag beginnt nach Beendigung des Ausschreibungsverfahrens mit dem Datum des Zuschlages im Anschluss an eine derzeit bestehende Vorlaufdeckung. (Typ M) In der Haftpflichtversicherung beträgt die Deckungssumme je Schadenfall EUR 25.000.000 pauschal für Personen-, Sach- und Vermögensschäden, einschließlich der Leistungen aus der Umwelthaftpflichtversicherung. In der Planungshaftpflichtversicherung steht eine separate Deckungssumme je Schadenfall von EUR 10.000.000 pauschal für Sach- und Vermögensschäden zur Verfügung. Die vorgenannten Summen sind dreifach maximiert. Die Extendend Maintenance im Teil Bauleistungs- und Montageversicherung beträgt 42 Monate. Die Nachhaftung beträgt in der Haftpflichtversicherung 10 Jahre, in der Umwelthaftpflicht- und Umweltschadenversicherung 5 Jahre. Der generelle Selbstbehalt beträgt mindestens EUR 25.000. Für Personenschäden entfällt der Selbstbehalt. In der Planungshaftpflichtversicherung ist die erweiterte Planungsdeckung eingeschlossen. Im Rahmen der erweiterten Planungsdeckung beträgt der Selbstbehalt EUR 100.000.

description: Doel is het volledig vernieuwen van de balansconstructie van de Oostelijke Noordkasteelbrug. Het vernieuwen van de balans van de Noordkasteelbrug is een ingreep om de initieel vooropgestelde levensduur te kunnen blijven garanderen. In grootte-orde bevat de scope van de werken aan de oostelijke brug: ­ Vernieuwen balansarm incl. windverbanden ­ Vernieuwen verbindingen balans en kist en mogelijk vernieuwen kist (+ vulling) ­ Vernieuwen trekstangen ­ Revisie en eventuele beperkte herstellingen (oa schokdempers) aan heugelbalken ­ Nauwkeurig inmeten van A, B, C en D scharnieren ­ Gedetailleerde weging van de vlucht ten einde de uitgangspunten bij ontwerp te kunnen verifiëren ­ Vervangen hoofddraaipunten Oostbrug (A+B+C+D lagers) cfr huidige configuratie ­ Optimaliseren alle lagers Oostbrug ­ Herstellen verankeringen A-scharnieren ­ Voorzien van secundair staal (leuningen, ladders, bordessen) zoals opgenomen in bestek ­ alle nodige demontage en montagewerken Met als randvoorwaarde de bestaande vluchten, stoel, heugelbalken, aandrijving en elektrische installaties te behouden. Naast de renovatiewerken aan de oostbrug dienen er wel enkele veiligheidsmaatregelen aan de westbrug te gebeuren; Deze omvatten beperkte aanpassingswerken aan secundair staal (leuningen, ladders, bordessen). Bijkomend kan de opdrachtnemer eventueel aangesteld worden voor het uitvoeren van dringende herstellingen aan de westbrug bij calamiteiten/storingen, dit gedurende de werken aan de oostbrug, teneinde onderbrekingen en stremmingen voor alle verkeersmodi tot een minimum te beperken.

title: Cybersicherheit von Betriebssystemen in software-definierten Fahrzeugen (SecAutomotiveOS)
description: Ziel des Projektes ist es, einen Gesamtüberblick über die im Fahrzeug eingesetzten eingebetteten Betriebssysteme (einschließlich Virtualisierungsumgebungen) und eine Bewertung der Cybersicherheitseigenschaften zu erhalten. Es sollen dabei die Einsatzbedingungen (Hardwareplattformen, Zugriffsmöglichkeiten auf Steuereinheiten usw.) und das Zusammenspiel der Betriebssysteme im Rahmen der Gesamtfahrzeugarchitektur einbezogen werden. Neben der Betrachtung der aktuell auf dem Markt befindlichen Systeme und einschlägiger Standards soll auch ein Ausblick auf die zukünftigen Entwicklungen gegeben werden. Anforderungen an Fahrzeug-Betriebssysteme aus Cybersicherheitssicht sollen aus den gültigen Regulierungen und Standards abgeleitet werden. Dies schließt Anforderungen an Prüfungen im Rahmen der Typgenehmigung und Marktüberwachung ein. Neben einer Quellenrecherche für den Marktüberblick sollen auch praktische Analysen an verschiedenen Betriebssystemen durchgeführt werden. Diese sollen im Rahmen des Arbeitspakets 5 (AP 5) durchgeführt werden. Der zu erstellende Prüfkatalog soll hier praktisch verifiziert werden können. Ergebnis des Projekts ist eine Studie, die die oben genannten Inhalte umfasst.

buyer: Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik
title: Projekt 1023: Prüfkriterien für Reinforcement Learning (RL-Criteria)
description: Das Projekt erarbeitet einen Katalog von Anforderungen, die der Bewertung der Sicherheit und Vertrauenswürdigkeit von Reinforcement Learning nutzenden KI-Anwendungen dienen. Die Anforderungen haben das Ziel, ein möglichst breites Spektrum an Anwendungen abzudecken. Dabei werden grundsätzlich alle Techniken und Ausprägungen von Reinforcement Learning, insbesondere auch im Zusammenhang mit großen und aktuellen generativen Modellen (Stichworte: RLHF, RLAIF), berücksichtigt. Die Anforderungen werden in der konkreten Ausarbeitung jeweils durch Erklärungen, begleitende Informationen, Umsetzungshinweise (z.B. Erläuterungen zum Einsatz geeigneter Testmethoden) u.ä. ergänzt. Der Katalog bildet damit eine Grundlage zur Selbsteinschätzung und zur Prüfung entsprechender KI-Systeme. Die im Projekt erstellten Anforderungen werden so aufbereitet, dass sie kompatibel zur SdT -Bibliothek des BSI sind und sich in das bestehende Produktportfolio des BSI zu KI-spezifischen Prüfkriterien einfügen. Konkret sind die Anforderungen abschließend als ergänzendes Modul zum BSI A5 zu gestalten.

Challenge sponsor: Department of National Defense (DND) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date: August 24, 2026 Closing date: October 5, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Challenge Problem statement The CA soldier will face an increasingly complex and dangerous battlespace in the future. A major element of the complexity and danger is the proliferation of multi-spectral sensors and precision weapons that will limit the CA’s ability to move cargo and strike enemy targets at range by using attributable ballistic trajectory weapons without the risk of being targeted and attacked. The CA presently lacks an UAS capable of conducting short-range cargo delivery of light supplies or remote munitions drops. The CA requires an innovative uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) that provides an uncrewed alternative to move combat supplies forward towards the frontline and to deliver munitions independent of predictable ballistic trajectories and launch signatures. This innovation must be simple, durable, and highly survivable, providing soldiers with an effective capability for future conflicts that integrates seamlessly into operations while minimizing training and maintenance requirements, allowing soldiers to focus on their mission. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution would: 1. Be composed of an: a. Air vehicle: The airframe containing the onboard electronics, propulsion, and payload. b. Sensor payload: The equipment required for navigation and to complete a mission, such as cameras or imaging systems. c. Ground control station (GCS): The system (laptop, tablet, or handheld controller) used by the human operator to control flight and manage missions. d. Radio: The wireless system that connects the GCS to the UAS to transmit commands and receive telemetry/data. e. Battery with charger: A battery for the UAS and a battery charger capable of charging multiple batteries simultaneously. f. Remote antenna: An external antenna placed 100m away from the GCS to enhance signal strength, reduce interference, and extend operational range. 2. Operate in various weather conditions, including at a minimum: a. temperature range of -20°C and +40°C; b. minimum windspeed of up to 40 km/hr; and c. light rain or snow ranging 0.5mm/m²/hr. 3. Be able to carry a minimum payload of 5kg of cargo. 4. Have a maximum takeoff weight than 25kg (includes payload). 5. Have both a minimum operational radius of 10km and an endurance of 30 min in continuous movement while carrying its payload. 6. Have vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) capability in a maximum area of 2m². 7. Be stowable in a 70-litre pack. 8. Be capable of operating at a minimum operational altitude of 1000 feet Above Ground Level (AGL). Additional outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Be deployable from a stowed state to a mission-ready state in 10 minutes or less. This includes the completion of all pre-mission preparation activities, including but not limited to unloading vehicle, loading/fueling the power system and loading/configuring mission set resulting in a vehicle that is fully mission-ready at the line of departure. 2. Have a sensor that enables the operator to recognize a target at a minimum distance under the following conditions: a. Day – Person (180cm) at 0.5km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 1km b. Night – Person (180cm) at 0.25km, Vehicle (5m x 3m x 2m) at 0.5km 3. Emit no more than 5 decibels Sound Pressure Level (dB SPL) of noise in all frequency ranges, measured at a 500m distance from the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV). 4. Be capable of operating with fibre-optic wire, or an alternate non-Electromagnetic (EM) spectrum means. 5. Incorporate Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) 256k encryption or equivalent for data transmission security. 6. Return to a pre-determined location, hover/loiter and/or climb in case of loss of link. 7. Have an aggregated projected production cost of $40,000 CAD or less per system. 8. Have a Ground Control Station (GCS) that: a. Incorporates a training simulation capability for Mission Planning. b. Has a minimum remote antenna cable length of 50m. c. Enables UAS navigation via both direct operator control and autonomously using waypoint navigation via the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). d. Displays the following information: - Location of vehicle in 6 figure Military Grid Reference System (MGRS); - Orientation of vehicle (pitch/roll/yaw); - Point of aim of camera in 6 figure MGRS; - Real-time full motion video feed; - Altitude in Metres above Sea Level (MSL); and - Battery life. e. Is capable of interfacing with the Tactical Assault Kit (TAK) battle management system to push UAS Position Location Information (PLI) and target PLI. 9. Have an alternate non-electric or hybrid power system capable of sustained operation beyond battery power (i.e. a gas-powered system or a gas/electric hybrid power system). 10. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies . title: TRAINING AND SUPPORT SERVICES FOR THE INTAC PROGRAM OFFICE
description: SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT � FOR INFORMATION ONLY Individual Terrorism Awareness Course (INTAC) 1. Introduction: This is a Sources Sought market survey for informational and planning purposes only, in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this announcement. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) � UMSB Contracting is conducting market research for the follow-on contract to support the Individual Terrorism Awareness Course (INTAC). The purpose is to identify parties who may be interested in and capable of performing this requirement. 2. Background: The INTAC program is a comprehensive, professional, resident training course that enhances the antiterrorism and force protection awareness posture of U.S. Army, Department of War (DoW), and other U.S. Government personnel. The course consists of a combination of classroom lectures and hands-on, performance-based training modules designed to provide realistic and challenging scenarios based on past events and current intelligence. The training prepares personnel who are considered to be at a medium-to-high risk from terrorism or criminal activity for their official travel and duties outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). 3. Requirement: The Contractor shall be required to provide all labor, equipment, materials, supervision, and contiguous training facilities necessary to conduct the INTAC training sessions and associated training modules. The core INTAC training is a multi-day session, supplemented by various optional modules that can be ordered as needed. See attached the DRAFT PWS. The Contractor will be responsible for providing and maintaining all necessary facilities, including road courses with varied configurations, firearms ranges, non-lethal shooting facilities, classrooms, and administrative and storage space for Government-furnished property. 4. Proposed Contract: The proposed contract is anticipated to be a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) with a five-year ordering period. The estimated contract ceiling is approximately $10,000,000. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 611519, �Other Technical and Trade Schools,� with a size standard of $16.5 million. All business sizes are welcome to respond; however, small business vendors are highly encouraged. 5. Requested Information: Interested parties are requested to submit a capability package that is not a proposal but a statement regarding the company's existing experience and capabilities. Please include the following in your response: Organization name, physical address, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity ID. Socioeconomic Status (e.g., Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, etc.). A summary of your company's capability to perform and manage a contract of this scope and complexity. Include 3 examples of comparable work performed within the past five years, with a brief description, customer name(s) and contact information, and the dollar value. A description of the resources and personnel your company possesses to perform this work as the prime contractor. Discuss any services that would be subcontracted and the technical capabilities of those subcontractors. Your company�s current facility clearance status. Provide comments to the attached DRAFT PWS. 6. Specific Questions: In addition to the general information requested above, please provide detailed responses to the following questions. These responses will help us better understand your capabilities in relation to the specific needs of the INTAC program. Range and Type of Classes: Describe your experience providing a diverse range of training courses similar to those in the INTAC program, from basic firearms and driving to advanced modules like Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) and Vehicle Commandeering. How do you ensure curriculum remains current with evolving threats? Facilities and Environment: Detail your existing training facilities. Specifically address your capacity to provide multiple road courses (paved, unimproved, off-road), skid pads, varied firearms ranges (including "drive-and-shoot" ranges), and indoor non-lethal training areas that can be configured for realistic scenarios, all within 125 miles of the Pentagon. Instructor Training and Qualifications: What are your minimum qualifications and certification standards for instructors across the different training disciplines (driving, firearms, medical)? Describe your process for recruiting, training, and continuously evaluating instructors to ensure they are experts in their respective fields. Scalability of Classes: Explain your capability to provide a flexible and scalable training schedule. How would you accommodate both the core INTAC course for up to 30 students and concurrently offer smaller, specialized training modules for groups as small as 1-3 students on an as-needed basis? 7. Submission Details: This market survey is for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP). The Government will not award a contract based on this announcement. Interested companies shall respond to this Sources Sought synopsis no later than 1:00 P.M. ET on 5 October 2026 to Giorgiana Chen at Giorgiana.Chen@usace.army.mil and Douglas Pohlman, at Douglas.E.Pohlman@usace.army.mil. RFI questions are due by 1:00 P.M. ET on 18 September 2026.

title: Marine Corps Cyberspace Environment (MCCE) Operational Support Services (OSS) and Enterprise Artificial Intelligence (AI) Integration
description: The Marine Corps Systems Command (MARCORSYSCOM), Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS), is conducting market research to identify capable, innovative commercial partners to deliver comprehensive, enterprise-scale Information Technology (IT) Operational Support Services (OSS).
